video_title: This Rune Giant Deck is TOTALLY OVERPOWERED!!

clock 2:27 (ability running): the general claim he makes for the Hero variant — "It's just so crazy how good the Hero Berserker is against just like any singular unit. You're able to just basically take every single singular unit out off the board just so fast. Kind of ridiculous."
clock 2:37: plain 2-elixir deploy at (4, 13), left lane on his own half, at 10 elixir (deploy label; the HUD misread this as Barbarian Barrel).

clock 1:18: Berserker at (3, 15), on the river in the left lane, at 4 elixir — the winning card, with the enemy left tower falling 3470 -> 1163 in the next six seconds. "Okay, let's go for the Berserker. Let's Evo Zap this as well. Just keep this alive."
rune-giant: clock 1:48: played once and defensively, at (9, 12) centre-map on his own half while the opponent's Elixir Golem sat at (3, 12) and an Inferno Dragon at (5, 16) in the left lane — a kite with a building-targeting 4-elixir troop rather than a lane trade. Pre-announced twice: "If he goes for an E-Golem at the bridge, we will have to Rune Giant kite" (clock 1:52) and "we do have to kite this with the Rune Giant" (clock 1:48).

clock 2:47: the frame for the whole session — he is not sure the card carries itself: "there's a possibility that's not even all that good and it's just really good with these cards ... sometimes I get a little bit overexcited and maybe think the card is a little bit better than it is, but it was just super good in one deck, which makes it just look extremely strong."

I would rather just leak some Elixir right here. But the thing is, if I leak Elixir, he just waits till double, then we lose. So I I guess I'll just E-Barbs at the bridge." The enemy left tower goes 4858 -> 3555 over the next 15 seconds.
clock 2:04: he commits them only because he is holding the swarm answer — "We have Zap in case he has a Skeleton Army."

clock 1:56: he counts the Evolution cycle as part of the plan — "Okay, having the Evil [Evo] E-Barbs up next will be nice."

clock 1:18: calls a second one alongside the Berserker — "Let's Evo Zap this as well" — so he is on the Evolved version; the cast itself is not separable from the 2-elixir drop at clock 1:09.

Ryley's pre-planned answer is a kite, not a trade — "If he goes for an E-Golem at the bridge, we will have to Rune Giant kite" — and he then layers Mother Witch (1:46), Minions (1:37) and Heal Spirit (1:36) behind his tower against the split bodies.

bullets: X2zRpx5TN2U game 1 (clock 2:50-0:58, win): a 119-second readable slice against Elixir Golem beatdown (Skeleton King, Inferno Dragon, Arrows, Zap, a missed Rage). The deck's two cheap bodies do the work — Heroic Berserker's Savage Survival at clock 2:32 removes a Skeleton King for 3 elixir, and a 2-elixir Berserker at the bridge at clock 1:18 takes the enemy left tower from 3470 to 1163.

clock 2:16-2:07: the deck's answer to being capped at 10 elixir against beatdown is Elite Barbarians at the bridge with Zap held — "if I leak Elixir, he just waits till double, then we lose. So I I guess I'll just E-Barbs at the bridge ... We have Zap in case he has a Skeleton Army." That push takes ~1300 off the enemy left tower.

clock 1:48-1:36: the stated Elixir Golem plan is a Rune Giant kite at (9, 12) centre-map plus Mother Witch (2, 4), Minions (5, 5) and Heal Spirit (6, 8) layered behind the tower — a four-card defence that still concedes the left tower down to 1616 and an activated King Tower, so the deck defends a big push by out-cycling it rather than stopping it.

clock 2:47: Ryley's own caveat on the archetype — the Rune Giant may be carried by the shell rather than the reverse: "there's a possibility that's not even all that good and it's just really good with these cards."

new_deck.rationale: Its offence is cheap fast bodies dropped at the bridge off a defensive cycle — Elite Barbarians at (3, 13) at clock 2:07 and a 2-elixir Berserker at (3, 15) at clock 1:18 — with the 4-elixir Rune Giant as a tank-and-buff option rather than a beatdown win condition.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The shell is eight cards with no building and no big tank: Rune Giant, Heroic Berserker, Elite Barbarians, Mother Witch, Minions, Heal Spirit, Zap and Fireball. Its damage comes from fast attackers the Rune Giant enchants — Berserker's 0.6 s hit speed reaches her every-third-attack bonus almost immediately — so a 2-elixir troop at the bridge behind a 4-elixir tank threatens a tower on its own. The Heroic Berserker's Savage Survival (3 elixir, 4 s of unkillable ultra-fast attacks at -75% tower damage) gives the deck a spell-free answer to any single big unit, which is how Ryley removes a Skeleton King at clock 2:32 without spending a card. Defensively it has no building, so heavy pushes are kited (Rune Giant centre-map at clock 1:48, Elite Barbarians at clock 1:25) and out-cycled with Mother Witch, Minions and Heal Spirit — in this match that still cost the left tower down to 1616 hitpoints before the counterattack won it.
